method: Text made without language: Dante's Italian (pinned it_dante) is enciphered with the published Naibbe cipher (naibbe_v2.py, commit 5145f52; 78-card deck, RESPACING=17, UNAMBIGUOUS=True, seed 0), which writes each plaintext letter or letter pair as a whole glyph group and does not keep word boundaries. On top of the cipher a scribe writing the book page by page keeps a list of words already written on the current page and, with probability 0.25, writes one of them instead of the next cipher token (30 per cent of copies carry one glyph change); the list resets at each page break. There is no section term anywhere: the process knows nothing about what the page is about or which section it belongs to. The text is written once and laid on every page of the manuscript in order (cut book), so F-018's section mutual information is measured on the same pages as the manuscript's. It is the text of R-051, which reproduced F-018 on the hidden pages (9/28). The point of the attack is that a page-local memory alone makes pages look section-structured: the null shuffles words across pages, which destroys page-level clusters, so page clusters pass a section test. No four-word run is copied from the manuscript; 5,225 lines, 34,183 words.
